Ravi (CS): NovaHealth seeing a sudden spike of 429s after they moved calls into short-lived lambdas. Need quick help, renewals at risk if this persists.

Onboard-Bot: Ticket NOV-512 created and linked.

Theo (Solutions): is this pure on-demand lambda or provisioned? SDK/runtime?

Ravi (CS): Python SDK v1.8.2, on-demand. Log sample: `2026-03-21T08:14:02Z POST /v1/completions 429 Retry-After:3 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0` then many near-simultaneous retries.

Lina (Eng-Support): classic cold-start stampede: many invocations refresh tokens and immediately issue requests. Quick mitigations: token cache in /tmp + file lock, respect Retry-After, add jitter to backoff.

Theo (Solutions): also recommend reusing a global http client to preserve keep-alive between invocations. If they cant provision concurrency, a small in-function queue or single outbound worker helps.

Ravi (CS): they can change function code. prefer minimal changes.

Lina (Eng-Support): i'll prepare a hotfix branch for the Python SDK (v1.8.3-lambda-cache) that: writes token to REDWOOD_TOKEN_CACHE_PATH (default /tmp/redwood-token.json), uses advisory file lock to prevent stampede, exposes REDWOOD_RESPECT_RETRY_AFTER=true, and enables jittered exponential backoff.

Theo (Solutions): good. for the customer call ask them to run a short canary with the hotfix and capture CloudWatch showing token fetch timestamps and X-RateLimit-* headers.

Ravi (CS): they ran a manual test: patched function to reuse global client and limited burst concurrency -> 90% fewer 429s.

Lina (Eng-Support): solid signal. i'll include telemetry in hotfix to log token_cache_hit=true/false so we can quantify the impact.

Onboard-Bot: PR sdk-py-1.8.3-lambda-cache created and linked to NOV-512.

Ravi (CS): scheduling 30m with their infra lead tomorrow to validate canary and ask their network/security about long-term fixes (provisioned concurrency or a tiny warm pool). Will update thread after canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
